subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How many pairs of chromosomes are found in the nucleus of a normal human body cell?
questions.explain: Human body cells contain 23 pairs of chromosomes, giving 46 chromosomes in total.

questions.q: Which pair of sex chromosomes is found in the cells of a human male?
questions.explain: Human males have one X and one Y sex chromosome (XY), whereas females have two X chromosomes (XX).

questions.q: What is a gene?
options: A section of DNA that codes for a protein
A single sugar molecule in DNA
questions.explain: A gene is a short length of DNA that codes for a particular protein.

questions.q: What is meant by the genome of an organism?
options: The entire genetic material of that organism
The proteins made by a cell
questions.explain: The genome is the complete set of genetic material (all the DNA) of an organism.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a dominant allele?
options: It is expressed even when only one copy is present
It is only expressed when two copies are present
It is never passed on to offspring
It is always found on the Y chromosome
questions.explain: A dominant allele is expressed in the phenotype whenever at least one copy is present.

questions.q: An organism is described as homozygous for a gene. What does this mean?
options: It has two identical alleles for that gene
It has two different alleles for that gene
It has only one allele for that gene
It has no alleles for that gene
questions.explain: Homozygous means the two alleles for a gene are the same (e.g. BB or bb).

questions.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
options: Genotype is the alleles present; phenotype is the observable characteristics
Genotype is the observable characteristics; phenotype is the alleles present
They both refer only to the physical appearance
They both refer only to the alleles present
questions.explain: The genotype is the combination of alleles an organism has, while the phenotype is the physical characteristics those alleles produce.

questions.q: Two heterozygous plants (Bb) are crossed. What proportion of the offspring are expected to show the recessive phenotype?
questions.explain: A Bb x Bb cross gives genotypes 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb, so 1 in 4 (25%) are homozygous recessive.

questions.q: A heterozygous organism (Bb) is crossed with a homozygous recessive organism (bb). What is the expected ratio of phenotypes in the offspring?
questions.explain: A Bb x bb cross produces half Bb and half bb offspring, giving a 1:1 phenotype ratio.

questions.q: Who is credited with proposing the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explain: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection.

questions.q: In which year did Charles Darwin publish On the Origin of Species?
questions.explain: Darwin published On the Origin of Species, setting out his theory of natural selection, in 1859.

questions.q: Which sequence best describes how natural selection leads to evolution?
options: Variation exists, better-adapted individuals survive and reproduce, passing on advantageous alleles
Individuals change their bodies during life and pass on those changes
All individuals in a population survive equally regardless of their alleles
Organisms deliberately choose helpful mutations to develop
questions.explain: Natural selection acts on existing variation, so individuals with advantageous alleles are more likely to survive, reproduce and pass those alleles on.

questions.q: Why can a population of bacteria become resistant to an antibiotic?
options: Random mutations produce resistant bacteria that survive and reproduce when the antibiotic is used
The antibiotic teaches the bacteria how to become resistant
Bacteria choose to become resistant when they are threatened
Resistance is passed from the patient to the bacteria
questions.explain: Chance mutations make some bacteria resistant; these survive the antibiotic and reproduce, so the resistant form spreads through the population.

questions.q: Selective breeding is also known by which name?
questions.explain: Selective breeding, in which humans choose which organisms reproduce, is also called artificial selection.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of genetic engineering?
options: Inserting the human insulin gene into bacteria so they produce insulin
Breeding the largest cattle together over many generations
Choosing the sweetest crops to plant next season
Allowing wild animals to compete for food
questions.explain: Genetic engineering involves transferring a gene from one organism to another, such as putting the human insulin gene into bacteria.

questions.q: Which of the following provides important evidence for evolution?
options: The colour of a painted wall
The number of leaves on a tree today
questions.explain: Fossils show how organisms have changed over long periods of time and are key evidence for evolution.

questions.q: What is the main source of new alleles (new genetic variation) in a population?
questions.explain: Mutations are changes to the DNA base sequence and are the source of new alleles and genetic variation.

questions.q: What is meant by the extinction of a species?
options: When no individuals of that species remain alive
When a species moves to a new habitat
When a species develops a new allele
questions.explain: Extinction occurs when there are no remaining living individuals of a species anywhere.

questions.q: A person has a scar from a childhood injury. This feature is an example of variation caused by which factor?
questions.explain: A scar results from an injury during the person's life, so it is variation caused entirely by the environment, not by genes.

questions.q: A homozygous tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a homozygous short pea plant (tt). What is the genotype of all the offspring?
options: A mixture of TT and tt
questions.explain: Each offspring receives a T allele from one parent and a t allele from the other, so all are heterozygous Tt.
